rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~91% 25bp / ~9% 50bp (CME FedWatch via Hercules); ECB Dec ~90%; BoE Dec ~80%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoC Dec ~44%; RBA 4.85%, hold expected
rows.read: Markets still treat a December Fed hike as close to certain, and a few soft US reports did not change that. The European Central Bank and Bank of England are also expected to hike, while Australian job losses suggest the Reserve Bank of Australia has peaked. US rates still look set to rise fastest, which keeps favouring the dollar.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: US claims 203K (fcst 198K); Philly Fed 6.3 (fcst 20.6); Conference Board LEI Oct −0.3% (fcst 0.0%); Australia jobs Oct −43.5K, unemployment 4.9%
rows.read: Several US reports softened at once: layoffs ticked up, a regional factory survey dropped sharply and a gauge of future activity slipped. Australia lost jobs for a second month. The US still looks firmer than most, but a run of soft figures would chip at the dollar's lead.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Philly Fed prices paid 58.2 (Oct 43.2); UK CPI Oct 3.6%; euro-area CPI Oct 4.0%
rows.read: Inflation is still well above target almost everywhere, which keeps most central banks leaning toward hikes. The prices US factories pay jumped this month, a sign that war-driven costs are still feeding through. That is why the Fed is slow to treat softer growth as a reason to stop.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: Anthropic share sale: foreign take-up est. $10–15B (Spectra Markets via Pound Sterling Live); GBP/USD −0.39%, AUD/USD −0.75%; USD/CHF +0.11%, USD/JPY +0.24% (Hercules)
rows.read: Heavy buying of US dollars, partly from foreign investors paying for shares in Anthropic's record stock listing, lifted the dollar against the pound and the Aussie. Gulf attacks continued, but markets took them in stride. The franc and yen got no safe-haven lift.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent $89.90, WTI $83.17 (+1.0%); gold $3,667.80 (−1.98%) (Hercules, New York close, indicative)
rows.read: Gold fell to its lowest in about 14 months, which weighs on the Aussie. Oil firmed a little but stayed near $90 for Brent, giving the Canadian dollar no real relief. Cheaper oil this month still helps importers like the euro area and Japan.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC report of Nov 10 (out late after Veterans Day): hedge funds for USD, GBP, AUD and gold; against EUR, NZD, CAD and CHF; slightly against JPY; real money disagrees on EUR, GBP and AUD
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds leaning toward the dollar and the pound and against the euro, the kiwi and the Canadian dollar, with bets against the kiwi growing fastest. Big long-term investors take the other side on the euro, pound and Aussie. Where the two groups disagree, a surprise could set off a fast unwind.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: ECB FSR: France debt 119% of GDP, deficit 5.5%; US October deficit $404B, a record for the month; US 10-year ~5.05% (Nov 19 close)
rows.read: France's debts, flagged by the European Central Bank as a risk, keep weighing on the euro. Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs near 5%, which weighs a little on trust in the dollar.
